subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats gain automatic durable per-sender dynamic agents, or should the supported boundary remain per-sender group session scopes plus explicit bindings/subagent spawns?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes durable agent creation, memory and skill isolation, group routing, hot config, quotas, and security boundaries, so automation should not choose the product shape.

options.title: Sponsor a Feishu plugin design
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a narrow Feishu-owned design covering sender identity, lifecycle, quota, memory/skill isolation, permissions, and live proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to existing primitives
options.body: Keep group isolation on current `group_sender` or `group_topic_sender` session scopes and explicit bindings/spawns, and document that automatic group dynamic agents are not supported yet.

options.title: Decline automatic group agents
options.body: Close the direction as too risky or too much orchestration for core/bundled Feishu, preserving manual routing and plugin extension discussions instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a Feishu plugin design
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a narrow Feishu-owned design covering sender identity, lifecycle, quota, memory/skill isolation, permissions, and live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is primarily product/security scope, and steipete is the best available owner signal from current main policy and recent source-area history.
